newsitem.title: UK: European bourses in record territory, lira firms.
newsitem.headline: European bourses in record territory, lira firms.

text.p: European bourses traded bullishly on Monday and Frankfurt broke records while the Italian lira, buoyed by re-entry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), strengthened against the mark.
London, Europe's biggest stock exchange, was at the day's high, 34 points or 0.8 percent up, in afternoon trade.
It extended a late Friday surge sparked by optimism over Tuesday's budget, a fresh outbreak of bid speculation and a Wall Street which saw an almost two percent rise over the course of last week.
On Monday the Dow opened flat but soon continued its rally. It was up 12 points at 6,484 in the European mid-afternoon.
Commenting on London's rise, one trader said: "It is incredible coming after Friday's move. The momentum has just carried on."
Index heavyweights Glaxo-Wellcome and British Telecom helped lead the gainers.
London analysts focused on the budget, hoping for a fiscally tight package that would ease pressure for higher interest rates to cool the pace of growth.

They saw the FTSE pushing towards its intraday record of 4,073.2 set on October 21. On Friday the blue chip index broke through 4,000 for the first time in November to close up 64.9 points, its biggest one-day gain in 16 months.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended floor trading at a record high, just below the psychological 2,800 barrier, and in after hours electronic trading the IBIS DAX index also nudged its previous trading peak.

The market was boosted by Deutsche Telekom, floated last week in the largest share sale in European history. It was the heaviest-traded stock and ended up three percent as initial profit taking waned.
German technical analysts said they remained bullish on the market's prospects for the remainder of the year and did not rule out the chance the DAX hitting 3,000 points early in 1997.
On the Paris bourse French shares traded well over one percent up as bulls continued to push the bourse higher, adding to its near one-percent climb on Friday.
Stock buying on the first day of the account helped, as did hopes of a continuation of Wall Street's succession of record highs, traders said.

Fire-hit Eurotunnel, however, was down eight percent after weekend reports that its re-opening for passenger traffic would miss the lucrative Christmas period, with only freight being allowed through the link for months to come
On the foreign exchanges, the lira rallied in reaction to the announcement late on Sunday that it had re-joined the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) at a 990 per-mark mid-point.
Italy had been ejected from the ERM in 1992 by a wall of foreign exchange bets against the lira.

Early on it firmed to within a whisker of its new central rate at 990.15 per mark, from around 999 late on Friday, before slipping a little to around 992 in the European afternoon. "I think a lot of the good news has been priced in for the lira, so I would be surprised if there was much more large-scale buying of lira," said a trader at a Swiss Bank.
Meanwhile, the dollar was in buoyant form above 112 yen and well over 1.51 marks and dealers said it was riding on the back of lira developments.
"The lira is strengthening. Money is flowing out of the Deutsche mark and this is having an effect on the dollar," said Elizabeth Legge, London-based economist at Bankgesellschaft.

On the bullion market, gold sank to its lowest level since March 2, 1995 and market professionals were betting it would dip further. Gold was fixed at $375.10 per ounce, down from $377.00 on Friday. It was the lowest fixing since $374.75 in March 1995.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.47 yen and 1.5185 marks against 111.34 yen and 1.5039 marks late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 33.7 points at 4,052.4.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 21.52 at 2,276.99.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 35.5 at 2,799.19.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $375.10, down from Friday's close of 377.15. Silver was down five cents at $4.84.
